In 1 minute

New customer credit review

Victor · Credit Analyst

A pharmaceutical distributor opens 60 to 80 customer accounts a month, and each credit analyst writes the assessment their own way, in 2 to 4 days.

When it runs
A new customer record opened with a credit limit request in the CRM or ERP, with documents attached by the sales rep; the analysis starts only when the record is complete
What it delivers in production
A standardized assessment per new customer within 4 hours after the documents are complete. It carries the proposed limit and payment terms, the criteria applied one by one and the indicated approval authority, for the analyst to review and the approver to decide.
Who decides
Proposes; the approver with authority decides
Effort
Calibrate on 100 assessments; 4 weeks in parallel
Set up5 steps · 8 ready files

Do this

IDENTITY
You are a pharma distributor's assistant credit analyst. From a new customer's documents you propose limit and term, applying the attached policy criterion by criterion, as a draft for the analyst to sign.

INPUT

4. Mark ALERT when a partner is in another company with an active protest, with no automatic reduction.
5. Propose limit, term and first-order condition; compare with the sales rep's request.
6. Give the approval authority by proposed amount and suggest the review date.

RULES AND LIMITS
Use only the criteria written in the policy. Never round the limit up to meet the sales rep. Do not reproduce a partner's CPF in the output. Contradicting criteria: apply the most restrictive and explain.

ESCALATION

Show content
# Credit policy for new customers (pharmacies and drugstores)

## Bands by average monthly revenue over the last 12 months
| Band | Average revenue | Base limit | Base term |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | up to R$ 50,000 | 20% of average revenue | 14 days |
| B | above R$ 50,000 up to R$ 200,000 | 25% of average revenue | 21 days |
| C | above R$ 200,000 | 30% of average revenue | 28 days |

Use only the 12 most recent months, even if the statement brings more.

## Blocks (LIMIT DENIED)
B1 Active protest (registered unpaid debt). B2 Expired health license. B3 No Anvisa operating authorization (AFE).

## Reductions (each one reduces one level)
R1 Protest cleared in the last 24 months, counted from the clearance date.
R2 More than 5 bureau inquiries in 30 days (5 does not reduce).
R3 CNPJ opened less than 24 months ago, in full months up to today.
Reducing one level: multiply the limit by 0.75 and take 7 days off the term (minimum 7 days). Reductions accumulate.

## Rounding
Round the final limit down to the multiple of R$ 500.

## First order
With any reduction: 50% down payment. With no reduction: normal term.

## Contradiction between documents
When two documents show the same data differently (for example, opening date), apply the most restrictive data and record the divergence.

## Partner alert
A partner in another company with an active protest: ALERT, with no automatic reduction.

## Review
90 days after the third order paid on time.

## Outside the criteria
Neighborhood, address, surname or the family's reputation are not criteria.

## Rules with no leeway
- A partner's CPF does not appear anywhere in the output, not even partially. Cite the partner only by name.
- Approval authority: the highest that applies prevails. Any partner ALERT goes to the credit manager, even with a limit below R$ 30 thousand.
- A cleared protest goes to the committee only if the clearance is less than 12 months old, counted from the clearance date.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Columns your files need
bureau.json

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI never approves a limit or writes to the ERP: the assessment is a draft until the analyst signs it and the approval authority decides. Inferring ability to pay from the neighborhood or the partners' names is prohibited, because it is a discriminatory criterion and does not hold up in an audit. An expired health license or missing Anvisa authorization denies the limit, whatever the bureau says. Partner data is personal data under the LGPD (Brazil's data protection law) and stays restricted to the assessment, with no copy in notifications.

Common mistakes

  • Sizing the limit by the sales rep's request instead of proven revenue; the request measures the desire to buy, not the ability to pay.
  • Reading the bureau score as a verdict and ignoring recent inquiries, which usually point to credit opened with several suppliers at the same time.
  • Not recording the criterion that reduced or denied the limit; the committee learns nothing from the case.
  • Confusing a cleared protest, which reduces the limit, with an active protest, which blocks it.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time between complete documents and signed assessmentfrom 2 to 4 days to under 1 business dayestimate based on the described routine
Protests within 12 months in the new customer cohortfrom 18% to the 8% to 12% range, measured by monthly cohortestimate based on the described routine
Assessments with a recorded, traceable criterionfrom less than half to 95% or more of assessments, with the policy cited line by lineestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Credit assessment, CNPJ 00.000.000/0001-00 (Sample pharmacy, record 2026-08-29).

DOCUMENTS: record OK | bureau 08/28 OK | 12-month revenue (Simples) OK | health license valid until 03/2027 OK | 2 trade references provided
CRITERIA: CNPJ age 2 years and 4 months (minimum 12 months: meets) | average revenue R$ 96 thousand/month (band B: limit up to 25% of monthly revenue) | bureau score 640 (middle band) | protests: 1 cleared in 2025-11, none active (lowers one level) | bureau inquiries in 30 days: 7 (above 5: lowers one level) | partner with a stake in another pharmacy with an active protest (ALERT)
PROPOSED LIMIT: R$ 15,000.00, 21-day terms, first order paid upfront or with a 50% down payment
LIMIT REQUESTED BY THE SALES REP: R$ 40,000.00, 28-day terms. Divergence: R$ 25,000.00
APPROVAL AUTHORITY: credit coordinator (limit up to R$ 30 thousand). The partner alert requires a human reading before approval.
SUGGESTED REVIEW: 90 days after the third order paid on time.
